title: test(plugin-grid,plugin-view): explainDouble answers a single-`recordId` request
body:
Fixes #9813

Both shared `explainDouble` helpers spread a `records` array only when the request carried `recordIds`. A single-`recordId` request — the shape `useRecordEditable` sends — came back with `allowed`, `object`, `operation`, `principal` and `layers`, and **no `record` member at all**. That hook reads `decision.record.visible` and returns early when it is not a boolean, so through either helper it took exactly the path it takes on a refused connection: the escape these helpers exist to close, reproduced inside them, and the opposite of the sentence their own docblocks carry.

Both copies now answer both shapes the explain hooks read, and take an optional row verdict so a suite can ask either of them for a DENY without hand-rolling a second double. `allowed` stays `true` throughout — it is the OBJECT-level verdict, and an object-level permit beside a row-level deny is exactly the sharing-rule case the hook was written for.

## Re-derived, not cited

**The card's line addresses still hold** on `origin/main` at `4b5772299` for plugin-grid's copy; plugin-view's equivalents sit three lines lower, because its docblock is longer.

**The two copies are still NOT identical, and the card's md5 pair reproduces exactly** — `2650630ec956f495e7a87e2fe599e0f2` (plugin-grid) against `3cd7e361f8bda009e79005b8f151f60d` (plugin-view). The card printed those hashes but explicitly did not diff them; this branch did. ⭐ **Every byte of the difference is docblock prose — the executable code was byte-identical**, so one patch genuinely applied twice. What differs: plugin-view cites objectui#4688 where plugin-grid cites #4296, wraps its paragraphs differently, carries an extra paragraph calling itself a per-package copy, and omits both plugin-grid's pointer to `rowRecordCrudVerdict.test.tsx` and its `__clearRecordCrudVerdictCache` sentence. After this change the install-docblock sentence is the only remaining difference; the rest were rewritten on both sides in step.

## There is a THIRD copy, and it is the one that was already right

`packages/test-support/src/record-security-explain-double.ts` answers the same route and already returned `record` for a single `recordId` and `records` for a batch. Found by listing every tracked path matching `double` case-insensitively — which returned the two subjects, this third one, one `.changeset` entry and one unrelated double-click test, so the search was lit rather than narrow. Its shape is what this change adopts, which is why the repair needed no design decision.

## What was passing because of this, and what happened once the double told the truth

⭐ **Nothing was passing because of it — the defect was LATENT rather than live.** That is the card's own headline open question, and it decides the grading.

Measured by instrumenting BOTH helpers to log every request they answered and running every file that imports either one: **75 explain calls, every one of them a batched `recordIds`, zero singular.** The batched count is the lit control for that zero, inside the same command.

⚠️ An earlier run of the same probe reported zero for both — that was the probe's fault, not a reading. This repo's configured vitest reporter prints no console output at all; `--reporter=default` is required to see any. A confident zero from the first shape would have been wrong in the worst direction.

⇒ no consuming suite ever took the singular path, so no suite's verdict was resting on the fail-open. After the repair those same 13 files are **13 passed / 152 tests** — identical to before. With the two new pins and the two verdict-agreement suites added: **17 passed / 184 tests**, all green. **Nothing reddened.**

## The pin, and what it is honestly worth

Each copy gains `explainDouble.singleRecordVerdict-9813.test.tsx`, which drives the real `useRecordEditable` unmocked, through the double, and asserts the decision it reaches — not the helper's shape.

- **The DENY leg is the pin.** Red without the repair: with no `record` member the hook fails open to `true`.
- ⚠️ **The PERMIT leg is a direction CONTROL, not a pin, and the file says so.** It was green before the repair too, because the hook initialises its verdict to `true` and its fail-open path leaves it there, so a permitted answer and an absent one are the same value at that read site. It stays because it fails the other way: a helper that started answering DENY by default would silently narrow every consuming suite, and that lands here.
- A third leg pins the batched shape and that `allowed` does not move with the row verdict.

### Ablations — both copies, one at a time, both pins run each time

| leg | mutation | plugin-grid pin | plugin-view pin |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | delete the singular spread from **plugin-grid's** copy | DENY leg FAILS — `expected true to be false` | 3 passed |
| 2 | delete the singular spread from **plugin-view's** copy | 3 passed | DENY leg FAILS — `expected true to be false` |

Each leg proved the mutation on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob hash moved) and proved the restore by blob equality against HEAD plus an empty `git diff HEAD`, with the restore armed on EXIT/INT/TERM against an absolute path. The PERMIT and batched legs stayed **green** under both mutations — predicted in advance, and reported because a green where red was expected would itself be the finding.

No `dist` preflight applies: both helpers and the consumer resolve from source through the root vitest alias map, so nothing had to reach a built artifact.

## Verify

All heavy runs through the shared lock, reading its VERDICT line rather than a bare status.

| run | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the 13 importing suites + 2 new pins + `rowRecordCrudVerdict` + `useRecordEditable` | `Test Files 17 passed (17)`, `Tests 184 passed (184)`, VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| `turbo run type-check` for both packages (builds their dependency closure) | `Tasks: 18 successful, 18 total`, VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| `turbo run lint` for both packages, re-run at final HEAD `3847c52e4` | `Tasks: 3 successful, 3 total` — 0 errors in all three tasks; zero findings naming any file this branch touches, against 1266 warning lines in the same log as control |
| `check-control-bytes` · `check-lint-coverage` · `check-changeset-presence` · `check-changeset-no-major` · `check-pending-changeset-literals` · `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` · `check-phantom-dependencies` · `check-test-path-roots` · `check-vi-mock-specifiers` · `check-vi-mock-inherit` · `check-vi-mock-override-shape` · `check-unreferenced-sources` · `check-changeset-claims` | every one exit 0, exit code captured before any pipe |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over this branch's five paths | `NOT GOVERNED — 5 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched` |

The full-farm runs — `pnpm test`, repo-wide `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check` — are CI's and are declared here rather than run locally.

A hand scan for control bytes over the five changed paths is silent, with a deliberately dirty file in the same command firing to prove the pattern is lit.

## Changeset: EMPTY frontmatter, and why

`.changeset/9813-explain-double-single-record-verdict.md` declares no bump. Measured rather than assumed: both packages publish `dist`, both build tsconfigs exclude the `__tests__` directory, and after building each package `installExplainDouble` has zero hits anywhere under either `dist` while a published symbol from the same package hits in the same command. The presence gate agrees in its own words — 4 source files of 2 released packages changed, 1 changeset, empty frontmatter, "the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate". This matches the convention the pending `explain-double-wire-shape-7996.md` already set for the sibling repair.

⛔ No `skip-changeset` label was applied: in this repository that label object exists but nothing reads it, and the empty-frontmatter declaration is the mechanism.

### Pending-changeset sweep

`check-changeset-claims` read this branch's four non-changeset files against **1165 pending declarations that publish a body** and found none naming a file this change touches. ⚠️ Two of its three readings are NOT clean verdicts and it says so itself: the born-false corpus needs a pull-request event it cannot see from a local run, and the self-contradiction reading has nothing to judge because this branch's only changeset declares no bump. No other card's changeset was edited.

## Closing keyword

`Fixes #9813` — merging completes the card. The repair, the two unmeasured readings the card asked for, and the pin all land here, and **no real fail-open survives in `useRecordEditable` as its own question**: that hook's fail-open is deliberate, documented on the hook itself, and already pinned by its own suite for the non-OK, throwing and no-verdict cases. The defect was entirely in the doubles. ⇒ no production permission change is implied, so nothing needed a separate fence.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, observed, deliberately not filed:

- **Three doubles answer one route.** The two subjects plus `@object-ui/test-support`'s, which is the correct one and is already imported by eight suites across five packages. Consolidating the two package-local copies onto it is a real simplification but a 13-file change with a different helper API (no call log, no echoed `object` / `operation` / `allowed` / `layers`). Whoever next touches either copy is the taker; there is no queued card that would reach these files.
- **plugin-view's docblock says there is "no repo convention for importing another package's test-only files across a workspace boundary".** Two `plugin-designer` suites already import plugin-grid's copy by relative path, so that sentence is falsified by the tree — but it was already false before this branch and this branch does not make it so, and correcting it is a judgement about repo convention rather than a defect repair. Left as written; the same relative route is what this branch's plugin-view pin uses, with its own reason stated in the file.
- **`AccessExplainPanel` in `@object-ui/app-shell` is the second production reader of the singular `decision.record.visible`** — the card asked whether one existed. It is not a consumer of either double (no app-shell test imports them), so it is unaffected here.
